articles.title: Pakistan's Kashmir And Indus Water Push: Is Islamabad Trying To Shift Focus From Terror? | News18
articles.description: Pakistan is once again bringing Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty into focus in its diplomatic messaging on India. But what is Islamabad really trying to achieve, and why is the question of cross-border terrorism missing from the public remarks of its visiting minister? Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik travelled to New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's Civilisational Dialogue Forum, held from November 20 to 22. Before the visit, Malik refused to rule out raising the Indus Waters Treaty dispute, even as he insisted that the forum was not a platform for bilateral negotiations. articles.title: Article 370 abrogation ended separatism among Kashmiri youth: Amit Shah
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said that the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth, and not a single local youth in the Valley is now involved in terrorism after 35 years of violence and unrest. He was addressing an event at Police Training Centre in Banderdewa near Itanagar in which the President's Police Colour was conferred to Arunachal Pradesh Police. "After over 35 years of violence, not a single local youth of Kashmir Valley is now involved in terrorism," he said. Recalling the troubled 90s, he said the situation in Kashmir Valley has undergone a sea change after the abrogation of Article 370. About criticism by opposition parties that the constitutional provision had no connection with terrorism, Shah said developments in the Valley have demonstrated otherwise. articles.title: Belgium raises 2027 work visa salary thresholds for foreign professionals, including Indians

articles.title: Bridge for a bridge? Russia's tit-for-tat strategy in Ukraine

The intensified focus on each other's critical infrastructure highlights the pivotal role of logistics in this ongoing conflict.
